items.title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion
items.summary: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation.

items.title: A Transdisciplinary Science of Information within the Organogram of Consciousness
items.summary: Information transcends the traditional disciplines of physics, psychology, cosmology, and biology, yet remains connected to them through Zero-Point Energy. Although the origins of space, time, and matter are known, the when and how of Information’s emergence remain elusive.
items.source: The American Journal of Applied Sciences

items.title: Multimodal Coma Stimulation to Improve Arousal and Physical Function in Patients with Traumatic Brain Injury
items.summary: Background: Impaired consciousness is one of the most serious complications following Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI). Sensory deprivation may delay neural recovery and worsen patient outcomes.

items.title: Quantum tomography of fermion pairs in e + e − collisions: Longitudinal beam polarization effects
items.summary: We present a quantum tomography study of fermion pair production at future e + e − colliders, emphasizing how longitudinal beam polarization controls the two-qubit spin density matrix. We study the processes e + e − → t t ‾ , e + e − → μ + μ − and Bhabha scattering e + e − → e + e − , representing the mass threshold behavior, the Z pole resonance and the s / t -channel interplay.

items.title: Nambu’s Dynamics, Strings, and Gravitized Quantum Theory
items.summary: In this article, we present a new view on string theory that is rooted in quantum foundations extended to the domain of quantum gravity in the form of gravitized quantum theory, in which the canonical probability measure captured by the Born rule of quantum theory, turns out to be dynamical and contextual. We claim that this gravitization of quantum theory is the essence of string theory.

items.title: Body in memory: the role of bodily self-consciousness in episodic memory and autonoetic consciousness
items.summary: Episodic memory (EM) enables the conscious recollection of personally experienced events, including contextual features such as visual, auditory and emotional details. However, the role of bodily signals has been largely neglected in EM, although the observer's body provides a rich bodily context during the encoding, storage and recall of events, and has recently been associated with a bodily form of self-consciousness (bodily self-consciousness; BSC).

items.title: CREST: A Hardware-Aware GNN-Based Framework for High-Fidelity and Robust Superconducting Quantum Compilation
items.summary: Quantum compilation on superconducting processors requires selecting a connected execution region whose topology and calibrated properties suit the input circuit. This choice constrains subsequent routing and influences the noise encountered during execution, yet aggregate hardware-quality metrics alone may not reliably predict the execution fidelity of a given circuit.

items.title: Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Learning
items.summary: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has attracted increasing interest as a possible route to construct feature representations that are difficult to reproduce with classical models. However, near-term QML architectures based on trainable parametrized quantum circuits remain affected by limited hardware resources, noise, and severe optimization difficulties such as barren plateaus.

items.title: A provably efficient classical algorithm for simulating OTOC$^{(1)}$ in 1D
items.summary: Out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) are quantities of broad interest in many-body physics due to their connection with information scrambling and quantum chaos. Recently, estimating higher-order OTOCs in random quantum circuits was proposed as a promising avenue for quantum advantage, yet the classical hardness of this task remains poorly understood.

items.title: Spontaneous emission of atomic systems near metallic and semiconducting atomic chains
items.summary: We investigate the spontaneous emission of a quantum emitter placed near finite atomic chains described by the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. By tuning the chain from a metallic to a semiconducting character through dimerization, we analyze how the electronic structure of an atomic-scale scatterer, together with the illumination profile, determines the strength, bandwidth, and spatial structure of the spontaneous emission enhancement.

items.title: Gradient Blindness in Adaptive Architecture Search for IQP Born Machines
items.summary: Instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) Born machines learn a probability distribution from data with a circuit of commuting gates that a classical computer trains at hundreds of qubits. Adaptive algorithms grow a sparse circuit from a small seed by adding in every round the candidate gates with the largest loss gradient.

items.title: Quantum Annealing with a Quantum Neural Network: Width of Annealing Matters
items.summary: Quantum annealing is a promising quantum algorithm for dealing with computationally hard optimization problems. Currently available hardware can implement the algorithm for a significant class of Hamiltonian problems.

items.title: Mind your head: Entropic Brain, irruption theory and the intelligibility problem
items.summary: Abstract The entropic brain hypothesis (EBH) and irruption theory (IT) are two recent frameworks to investigate consciousness by examining neural entropy. While they differ in their theoretical commitments, both aim to advance neuroscientific investigations of consciousness without succumbing to the intelligibility problem: the impossibility for scientific inquiries to provide intelligible access to subjective experience.

items.title: 100 ± Δ t years of quantum uncertainty: From origins to modern insights
items.summary: Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle is a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, marking a decisive departure from classical physics. Conceived almost a century ago through a thought experiment showing that measuring an electron’s position inevitably disturbs its momentum, it began as a deceptively simple idea that sparked countless studies and grew into the rich research field it is today.

items.summary: In anesthesia, and in emergency and intensive care medicine a “therapeutic communication” with the patient is needed that exceeds mere information exchange and that supports patient and treatment. First, ever-present nocebo effects and negative suggestions must be avoided or neutralized.

items.title: Early visual experience contributes to the calibration of higher-order body representations
items.summary: Higher-order body representations, including representations of body shape and size, play an important role in maintaining perceptual constancy in touch. However, whether the development of these representations depends on early visual experience remains unclear.

items.title: Conversing with a Conversational Agent: A Real Conversation, Not a Simulated One
items.summary: The claim that interactions with artificial conversational agents merely simulate human conversation rests on a philosophical distinction between reproducing the observable features of an activity and actually performing it. Although this distinction is appropriate for certain physical phenomena, its application to linguistic and symbolic activities is far less straightforward.

items.title: Noetics, a New but Old Understanding of Mind and Reality
items.summary: Noetics is examined here as an interdisciplinary approach to how lived experience becomes a knowledge claim and informs action. This narrative review brings historical philosophy into dialogue with cognitive science, contemporary theories of consciousness, contemplative traditions, and artificial intelligence.

items.title: Actualization and the Quantum Mechanical Universe: Dissolving the Gap
items.summary: The actualization gap—the apparent discontinuity between the classical probability distribution delivered by decoherence and the single definite outcome that appears in experience—has been treated in the foundations literature as an outstanding problem in the physics of quantum measurement. This paper argues that the gap is not a physical problem and admits no physical solution.

While previous work has demonstrated the dissipative stabilization of multimode Schr\"odinger cat states as robust quantum memories, a framework for universal quantum computation has remained unavailable.

items.title: Fixed-preparation short-time reconstruction of class-D BdG endpoint masses
items.summary: In one-dimensional class-D superconductors, the relative signs of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) masses at particle-hole-invariant momenta fix the bulkinvariant. Band energies and transition-frequency peak locations alone cannot determine these signs.

items.title: Residual Allan Stability under Periodic Auxiliary Ramsey Sampling
items.summary: The timing of auxiliary Ramsey measurements can change the frequency stability associated with a drifting pulse shift at a fixed nominal Fisher-information rate for a constant shift. For periodic instantaneous observations of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck shift with causal prediction between updates, we derive the exact residual covariance averaged over the update cycle and the corresponding Allan variance at arbitrary averaging times.

items.title: Epistemological Problems of Interdisciplinary Interaction between Philosophy and Cognitive Sciences (Reflection on the Book)
items.summary: This paper presents a panoramic sight of philosophical and methodological problems concerning interdisciplinary interaction of philosophy and cognitive sciences in the context of reflections upon Natalia Smirnova’s book “Imagination, Language, Creativity. Philosophy and Cognitive Sciences in the Study of Creative Activity of Consciousness” (Moscow, Saint Petersburg: Tsentr gumanitarnykh initsiativ, 2025).

items.title: Does Total Knowledge Mute Emotion? A Thought Experiment using Large Language Models
items.summary: Abstract This paper examines whether comprehensive knowledge acquisition attenuates emotional experience through a thought experiment that uses large language models (LLMs). We propose that LLMs, which possess extensive propositional knowledge yet lack phenomenal consciousness, serve as philosophical instruments for isolating the knowledge variable from other cognitive attributes.

items.title: Virtual reality as a neural state-modulating technology: EEG complexity during VR gameplay versus VR gameplay viewing
items.summary: Pharmacological agents and brain stimulation can modulate conscious states, but offer limited control over the structure of the experience itself. Virtual reality (VR) can alter subjective experience while allowing its structure to be experimentally controlled.

Setting down what our programs have learned so that others can use it, contest it, and test it, we work through the central tensions that every QISE graduate program must negotiate: between depth in a home discipline and breadth across the field, between structured…

items.title: Opposite post-processing orders of fermionic horizon channels and their quantum-resource monotonicity
items.summary: Abstract Studies of relativistic quantum information in noninertial and black-hole settings often focus on specific input states and resource functionals, leaving the common origin of recurring monotonic trends in quantum resources and correlations unclear. In this work, we identify a common channel-ordering structure from the complementary exterior and interior reductions of the effective single-mode fermionic horizon transformation, representing the physically accessible and inaccessible sectors, respectively.

items.title: Quantum Sensing as an Optimization-Inference Stack
items.summary: Every data science pipeline begins with a measurement. When that measurement is made by a quantum mechanical system—exploiting superposition, entanglement, and coherence—the sensor can in principle surpass the classical shot-noise precision limit.

items.title: Measurement-informed dynamical decoupling for fidelity preservation on large-scale quantum processors
items.summary: Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a key technique for suppressing decoherence and preserving the performance of quantum algorithms. We introduce a measurement-based DD (MDD) protocol that determines control unitary gates from partial measurements of noisy subsystems, with measurement overhead scaling linearly with the number of subsystems.

items.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) introduces substantial systems-level complexity through quantum error correction (QEC), making debugging FTQC programs challenging. Existing quantum debugging approaches primarily target logical-level circuits and do not naturally support debugging within realistic FTQC execution flows.

items.title: Almost-quantum correlations violate information causality
items.summary: Abstract Information causality (IC), a generalization of the no-signalling principle, states that communicating m classical bits cannot give the receiver access to more than m bits of information about the sender's independent data. Although IC holds in quantum theory and excludes a broad class of supra-quantum correlations, its validity for the almost-quantum set has remained open.

items.summary: How many distinguishable labels can a biological oscillator carry? Proposals invoking collective vibrational modes, endogenous electromagnetic fields, microtubule excitations and oscillatory phase codes are each debated on grounds particular to themselves, with no shared standard for comparison.

items.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
items.summary: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions.

items.title: Physical predictions in closed quantum gravity
items.summary: A bstract Recent developments in gravitational path integrals indicate that the nonperturbative physical Hilbert space of a closed universe is one-dimensional within each superselection sector. This raises a basic puzzle: how can a unique quantum-gravity state give rise to semiclassical physics, measurement outcomes, and classical probabilities?

items.title: Quantum Symmetry and Entanglement Horizons: Theory, Photonic Systems, and Quantum Inspired Data Analytics
items.summary: This book examines the role of translational symmetry in shaping and stabilising quantum entanglement across spatial and temporal domains. Building on foundational concepts from the EPR paradox and Bell’s theorem, it introduces a nodal–antinodal framework to explain coherence preservation and entanglement amplification.

items.title: Indefinite causal order with definite Bohmian trajectories for the quantum switch
items.summary: We analyze the notion of indefinite causal order (ICO) from the standpoint of the deterministic de Broglie--Bohm theory, based on the notion of trajectories in configuration space. More precisely, we study the physics of the quantum switch (QS) interferometer within a Bohmian framework and show how the notion of causality is preserved in this approach.

items.title: Quantum algorithms
items.summary: This chapter highlights quantum algorithms as a gate-based computational framework that exploits superposition, entanglement, and phase-coherent interference to realize demonstrable complexity reductions on selected problems. It begins by formally distinguishing quantum algorithms from classical deterministic and randomized computation through reversible unitary evolution, oracle-based problem access, and the measurement constraint that collapses quantum state information, thereby motivating amplitude-engineering…

items.title: Quantum Machine Learning: Theory, Algorithms, and Practical Implementation
items.summary: Quantum machine learning (QML) has emerged as a rapidly developing field at the intersection of quantum computing, artificial intelligence, and data science. As quantum hardware and algorithms continue to advance, there is a growing need for a rigorous and accessible text that explains how quantum principles can be used to design, analyze, and implement machine learning models.

items.title: Decoding sequence auditory expectations for clinical diagnostic and prognostic assessment of prolonged disorders of consciousness
items.summary: OBJECTIVE: Electroencephalogram (EEG) features are important objective markers for diagnostic and prognostic evaluation of prolonged disorders of consciousness (DOC). However, task-based EEG paradigms are limited by mismatches between task demands and patients' residual awareness, as well as the limited individual assessment capacity of machine-learning-based detection frameworks.

items.title: A Nonsecular Quantum Master Equation with Detailed Balance and Second-order Error Bound
items.summary: An effective theory of open quantum systems should preserve the detailed balance structure inherited from microscopic reversibility and remain accurate throughout relaxation. Meeting both requirements is particularly challenging in quantum many-body systems, where dense spectra can invalidate the secular approximation even at weak coupling.

items.title: Dressed-State Quantum Information Processing Using a Multilayer Ion Trap Chip with an Integrated Radio Frequency Resonator
items.summary: We present the experimental preparation of a radio frequency (RF)-dressed-state qubit, the coherent operation of a single RF-dressed qubit, and the selective readout of RF-dressed hyperfine states of $^{171}$Yb${^+}$ ions trapped using a novel microstructured ion trap chip. We demonstrate the individual addressing of RF-dressed-state qubits in a two-ion Coulomb crystal.

items.title: Residual-Algebraic Design of Symmetry-Preserving Variational Quantum Circuits
items.summary: Symmetry-preserving (SP) variational quantum circuits restrict evolution to physically relevant sectors of Hilbert space, but symmetry preservation alone does not guarantee accessibility within those sectors. We show that a restricted generator set can possess a residual dynamical Lie algebra whose commutant further decomposes the target symmetry sector into invariant blocks.

items.title: Quantum Simulation of First-Quantised Chemistry with a Sum-of-Squares Representation
items.summary: Calculating molecular energies is expected to be an important application of quantum computers, but the most efficient algorithms to achieve this typically have significant space requirements. Scaling quantum processors to thousands of logical qubits is a daunting engineering challenge, so developing algorithms that run with reduced qubit requirements is of particular importance.

items.title: Hurst Exponent Estimation with Quantum Wavelets
items.summary: How accurately can the Hurst exponent $H$ of fractional Brownian motion be estimated from repeated preparations of a single amplitude-encoded path, when every measurement interrogates the same realization? We extend the $ε$-decimated quantum nondecimated wavelet transform in three directions: we remove the endpoint jump of circular filtering, derive the sampling distribution of the estimator, and compare readouts at equal query budgets.

items.title: Time-Varying Medium from an Ensemble of Laser-Dressed Quantum Emitters
items.summary: We propose a minimal quantum-mechanical model of a frequency dispersive, time-modulated medium that explicitly incorporates the pumping mechanism. It consists of a homogeneous ensemble of quantum emitters dressed by a pump laser.

items.title: The limits of magic-state cultivation
items.summary: Fault tolerance is understood through Pauli algebra, which fails at non-Clifford gates. Circuits such as magic-state cultivation, which checks an encoded T state with physical T gates, have therefore lacked an exact theory of which faults are harmful.

items.title: Shedding Light on Quantum Non-Classicality: Witnessing Wigner Negativity with Free Electrons
items.summary: Certifying quantum non-classicality like Wigner negativity typically demands full optical state tomography. This work introduces a noise-resilient framework for witnessing optical Wigner negativity using phase-resolved quantum photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (QPINEM).

items.title: Environment-assisted imaginary time evolution in feedback-based quantum algorithms
items.summary: The Feedback-based Algorithm for Quantum Optimization (FALQON) prepares ground states without classical parameter optimization, but requires deep circuits and can stagnate away from the ground state as a consequence of barren plateaus and symmetry protection. In order to avoid stagnation, imaginary time evolution (ITE) layers can be incorporated into FALQON layers, enhancing FALQON convergence.

items.title: Squeezed Cooling and Lasing with Cold Atoms in Cavity-QED
items.summary: A squeezed laser undergoes a lasing transition into a squeezed cavity mode, where stimulated emission generates a bright coherent field with a laser-like coherence time while maintaining one field quadrature below the vacuum noise level. Here we propose an optical implementation that needs neither a nonlinear crystal nor injected squeezed light, based on engineered interactions between ensembles of rubidium atoms and a squeezed cavity mode via cavity-assisted Raman transitions.

items.title: The magical memory cost of entanglement spectrum compression
items.summary: How much quantum memory is needed to faithfully retain the entanglement spectrum of a bipartite pure state after separating out Bell pairs through local unitaries? We derive the exact tradeoff between Bell-pair yield, residual memory, and reconstruction fidelity under local unitaries, defining an operational measure of entanglement-spectrum complexity.

items.title: Coherent-Response and Thermal-Fluctuation Information in Cavity-Magnon Magnetometry
items.summary: Magnetic sensing with cavity--magnon systems typically relies on the coherent response, while field-dependent fluctuations are treated as measurement noise. Here, we show that the variance of a measured microwave quadrature provides a distinct source of magnetic-field information.

items.title: On Reaction Depth and Fast Fault-Tolerant Boolean Logic
items.summary: Reducing runtimes of quantum applications is critical for practical viability. On quantum computers, the runtime can depend both on the speed of quantum operations and on how often the program must wait for the classical coprocessor to determine adaptive operations.

items.title: Number-correlated photon entanglement with a quantum memory interferometer
items.summary: Strong photon-photon interactions are central to quantum optical technologies yet remain challenging to realise at the single-photon level. Here, we show how embedding a quantum memory within a Mach-Zehnder interferometer enables a coherent transformation that converts single-mode photon states into number-correlated entangled states.

items.title: Measurement-order dependence bounds uncertainty, contextuality, steering, and Bell nonlocality
items.summary: Two quantum measurements applied to the same input in opposite orders give two joint distributions of the same outcomes. For Lüders instruments we measure how far apart these order records can be, over all inputs, by their total-variation distance $\mathcal{T}$, their Jensen-Shannon divergence $\mathcal{J}$ (in bits), and their squared Hellinger distance.

items.title: No-Go Theorems for Ordered Universal Entanglement Purification
items.summary: Entanglement purification is a fundamental tool for obtaining high-fidelity entangled states used in various quantum technologies. It aims to increase the fidelity of noisy shared entangled states with a fixed maximally entangled state through LOCC.

items.title: Gutzwiller Quantum-Classical Embedding for Dynamics Simulations of Correlated Electron Systems
items.summary: Simulating the real-time dynamics of correlated electron systems requires a nonperturbative treatment of local correlations over long times, a challenge for classical methods. We present the time-dependent Gutzwiller quantum-classical embedding framework, t-GQCE, for generic multi-orbital lattice models with time-dependent Hamiltonians.

items.title: On a local hidden-variable model for postselected EPR correlations
items.summary: A theoretical and numerical analysis of a Bell-type experiment is presented, where linear polarization measurements on nonmaximally entangled two-qubit states are modeled through a sigmoid-based threshold mechanism that violates the fair-sampling assumption required by the CHSH inequality. Numerical simulations characterize how closely this local construction can reproduce quantum-like correlations in the postselected detected sample, for both the |Phi_r> and |Psi_r> states over a range of entanglement parameters.

items.title: A Relativistic Quantum Mechanical Formulation of Wu-Shaknov Entanglements
items.summary: It is suggested that a spontaneous formation of quantum mechanical entanglements does actually occur between spin, helicity and polarization states involved in creation-annihilation processes. A framework built up earlier that presumably affords a unified relativistic quantum mechanical description of free particle-antiparticle pairs of any spin is used to propose a comprehensive formulation of Wu-Shaknov entanglements.

items.title: Sharp rank thresholds and cubic support in PPT extensions of completely symmetric states
items.summary: For completely symmetric states on $d\ge3$ parties of actual local rank $N\ge3$, the least rank of an entangled state passing any prescribed finite positive level of the PPT extension hierarchy is $3d+N-3$. At equality, the two- and three-party marginals recover a ternary plane cubic shared by every extension.

items.title: A Bose-Hubbard quantum thermal machine
items.summary: This work proposes a quantum thermal machine comprised of interacting ultracold bosons confined in a one-dimensional optical lattice and modeled by the Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian. We consider an Otto-inspired cycle with strokes that change the interaction strength between bosons, in addition to standard thermalization and compression/expansion strokes.

items.title: Bound entanglement as a trigonometric moment problem
items.summary: Entangled states that are positive under partial transposition (PPT) are the main obstruction to a simple description of entanglement. We study three basic questions about them within a class of multiqubit states, the mixtures, with real but possibly negative weights, of products of equatorial spin coherent states of several groups of qubits: which PPT entangled states belong to the class, how robust their entanglement is to white noise, and how small their rank can be.

items.title: Linear-mode photon counting performance and intrinsic dark current in HgCdTe APDs for quantum optical applications
items.summary: The performance of HgCdTe APDs for single photon detection at T=80 K has been characterized using a hybrized Resistive Trans-Impedance Amplifier (RTIA) and a deported Capacitance Trans-impedance amplifier (CTIA). The single-photon detection capacity was characterized with the HgCdTe APDs operated in linear mode with high APD gain, M>400, and hybridized with the RTIA.

items.title: Virtual Autopurification in Translationally Invariant Quantum States
items.summary: We introduce virtual autopurification (VAP), a protocol for virtual purification that operates entirely within a single translationally invariant system. Virtual purification suppresses thermal fluctuations and decoherence noise by amplifying the dominant pure component of a mixed state, but its standard implementation requires multiple copies of the state and global entangled measurements.

items.title: A unified approach to the time-dependent quantum harmonic oscillator via point transformations and Lie symmetries
items.summary: We revisit the time-dependent harmonic oscillator (TDHO) in quantum mechanics based on the notion of equivalence transformations and Lie point symmetries. Within this framework, we give the most general point transformations depending on seven parameters which map from the TDHO to the usual harmonic oscillator (HO) and the other way around.

items.title: Efficient simulation of variational quantum circuits: representation, accuracy and CPU/GPU allocation
items.summary: Classical circuit simulation supports quantum software development and verification and provides a baseline for assessing quantum advantage. We compare gate-based statevector simulation, direct Pauli evolution and matrix product states for molecular and spin Variational Hamiltonian Ansatze and hardware-efficient ansatze on CPU/GPU systems, varying width, depth, precision and resource allocation.

items.title: Long-distance continuous variable entanglement distribution over deployed fibre
items.summary: Continuous-variable (CV) entanglement offers deterministic generation and room-temperature coherent detection for quantum networks, but distributing it over deployed fibre has been hindered by the need to stabilise optical phase, polarisation, and timing at remote receivers. Here we demonstrate, to our knowledge, the first distribution of CV entanglement over deployed metropolitan fibre using independent coherent receivers.

items.title: Doppler effect on dual-downlink time-bin quantum key distribution and a proposed ephemeris-assisted witness-field correction
items.summary: Time-bin entanglement is promising for satellite Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) due to its compatibility with telecom fiber networks, but its phase-sensitive measurements are vulnerable to Doppler effects induced by satellite motion. We present a spectral-temporal framework for time-bin-entangled photon pairs generated onboard a satellite via Spontaneous Parametric Down Conversion (SPDC) and distributed to two Optical Ground Stations (OGSs) over independent downlinks with distinct Doppler shifts.

items.title: QuFrame: Pauli Frame Tracking for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Control
items.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires continuous quantum error correction (QEC) to suppress physical noise. While Clifford-only workloads can defer corrections to software post-processing, universal computation breaks this paradigm: executing non-Clifford gates via magic-state gadgets introduces hard, real-time control-flow dependencies on error-corrected measurements.

items.title: A Convex-Roof Affinity-Square Measure of Quantum Imaginarity
items.summary: Quantum imaginarity characterizes the part of a quantum state that cannot be represented by real density matrices in a fixed reference basis. We study an affinity-square measure of imaginarity for pure states and its convex-roof extension to mixed states.

items.title: Quantifying extractable imaginarity with qubit triangles
items.summary: Two qubit states with the same robustness of imaginarity can differ in the robustness attainable by real filtering on a successful outcome. We represent the input robustness $R$ and the largest conditional robustness $κ$ by the base of a right triangle and the slope of its hypotenuse, respectively.

items.title: Semiclassical Quantum Mechanics and the Optics of Time-Varying Media
items.summary: Rapid, high contrast modulation of optical parameters such as the refractive index can radically reshape a wave's frequency spectrum as it propagates. Non-commuting frequency and time operators can be used to describe this reshaping, analogous to the position and momentum operators of quantum mechanics.

items.title: Beyond Corpus-Driven Imitation: Evolving Musical Mindsets in the Agentic Orchestra via Quantum Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper presents a framework for computer-aided music composition and performance based on quantum reinforcement learning and multi-agent interaction. We introduce the agentic orchestra, where musical agents evolve distinct mindsets through trial-and-error engagement with a musical environment, rather than through training on large datasets.

items.title: In-memory measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution
items.summary: Quantum memories offer to significantly extend the performance of quantum networks, but their complexity and limited performance at telecommunication wavelengths have so far hindered practical deployment. We propose a new memory-assisted measurement device independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) protocol based on in-memory interference.

items.title: A relativistic gravitisation of quantum theory?
items.summary: We develop a model, that we call local semiclassical gravity, based on the distributional semiclassical Einstein field equations (EFEs) sourced by the local quantum state, i.e. the reduced density matrix of the local system updated by collapses (only) in its past light cone.

items.title: Quantum Parallel Algorithm for Multivariate Trace Estimation with Applications
items.summary: Estimating multivariate traces Tr(A1A2......Ak) is a fundamental task arising across diverse fields. In this paper, We develop a quantum algorithm for this problem tailored to near-term quantum devices.

items.title: Stabilizer models of achiral abelian topological orders
items.summary: We construct continuous-variable stabilizer codes realizing every achiral 2D abelian topological order, both bosonic and fermionic. Starting from an arbitrary signature-zero integer $K$-matrix, we show that the corresponding topological order can be obtained by condensing a lattice of dyons with trivial pairwise mutual braiding in an $\mathbb{R}^N$ gauge theory.

items.title: CCZ gate beyond the strong Rydberg-blockade regime
items.summary: We present a protocol for implementing a controlled-controlled-Z (CCZ) gate on a neutral-atom platform, employing three individually addressable atoms confined in a linear array of optical tweezers and operating under finite Rydberg-Rydberg interaction (RRI). The protocol combines successive excitation of the Rydberg atoms with analytically determined pulses and uses two Rydberg levels to access opposite-sign interaction shifts.

items.title: Reliability of quantum communication over erasure channels
items.summary: Quantum information can be reliably transmitted at rates below the quantum capacity with an error that vanishes as the number of channel uses grows. The reliability function characterizes the optimal exponential decay rate of this error.

items.title: Odd-Even Effects on Liouvillian Spectra and Relaxation Dynamics in Boundary-Driven Spin Chains
items.summary: We investigate odd-even effects on Liouvillian spectra and relaxation dynamics in boundary-driven XY and cluster chains. With the bulk couplings and boundary dissipation rule fixed, the parity of chain length determines whether non-decaying oscillatory modes exist.

items.title: Accelerating Quantum Error Correction Simulations under Coherent Noise with Compiled Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product States
items.summary: Reliable assessment of quantum error correction requires understanding how coherent errors affect logical performance. Although tensor networks naturally capture coherent interference, entanglement growth and large qubit counts make repeated sampling costly.

items.title: Vanilla Adiabatic Quantum Optimization Can Have Subexponential Advantage
items.summary: We construct a family of objective functions $f \colon \{0,1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ for which vanilla adiabatic quantum optimization along $H(s) = -(1-s)\sum_{i=1}^n X_i + s\sum_x f(x)\lvert x\rangle\!\langle x\rvert$ finds the global minimizer in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time, whereas any classical algorithm requires $\exp(n^{Ω(1)})$ time to do so in the black-box model. Our result is achieved by replacing the linearization technique in an earlier work of Leng et al.

items.title: Distinguishing Conserved Quantum Sectors via Measurement Record Features
items.summary: Conservation laws partition the Hilbert space of a quantum system into invariant sectors that are often difficult to identify directly. Repeated measurements on an ancillary probe, however, generate a measurement record that provides information about the occupied sector.

items.title: Topological Quantum Reservoir Computing
items.summary: Scaling universal quantum computation and implementing quantum machine learning with protected logical qubits remain challenging. To harness the computational potential of existing fault-tolerant quantum platforms, we introduce topological quantum reservoir computing, a novel approach using protected degrees of freedom for storage and the host system's intrinsic dynamics for information processing.

items.title: Topological Origin of Directional Amplification in Arbitrary-Dimensional Non-Hermitian Lattices
items.summary: In non-Hermitian lattices, combinations of gain, loss and nonreciprocal couplings can generate exponentially growing directional amplification with applications in signal processing and precision measurement. An intriguing question is whether such amplification has a universal topological origin in arbitrary dimensions.

items.title: Efficient Spectra and Dynamics with Tangent-Space Chebyshev Tree Tensor Networks
items.summary: We present a tangent-space Chebyshev method (TaChe), which combines tree tensor network states with Chebyshev recursion and maximum entropy spectral analysis in a tree tensor network tangent space, for quantum many-body spectra and dynamics. Implemented tensor network state calculations in the tangent space of the ground state, the core advantage of TaChe is that it can substantially reduce the computational complexity, memory usage, and numerical instability associated with tensor network state compression.

items.title: Quantum Mpemba effect in a driven-dissipative atom-waveguide coupled system
items.summary: The quantum Mpemba effect (QME) describes the counterintuitive phenomenon in which a more strongly perturbed quantum system relaxes toward its steady state faster than a less perturbed one. Here, we investigate the QME in a weakly driven-dissipative atomic array coupled to a one-dimensional chiral waveguide.

items.title: Analysis of a Homodyne-Like Measurement Scheme Using Photon Counters and Weak Local Oscillator
items.summary: In standard homodyne detection, an unknown optical signal state is combined with a local oscillator (LO) at a beam splitter (BS), and the appropriately integrated intensities at the two outputs of the BS are subtracted to obtain an approximate quadrature measurement. Accurate quadrature measurements require a high-amplitude LO and high-efficiency detectors.

items.title: The $S$ and Double-Exponential Transformations with a Moment Expansion for Three-Centre Coulomb and Hybrid Integrals
items.summary: Three-centre two-electron Coulomb and hybrid integrals over exponential-type functions involve semi-infinite radial integrals containing oscillatory spherical Bessel functions. We investigate the combination of the $S$ transformation with Fourier-type double-exponential (DE) quadrature for their accurate and efficient numerical evaluation.

items.title: Faster than square-root run-time in adiabatic quantum algorithms for Exact Cover 3
items.summary: By intertwining ideas from sequential and adiabatic quantum computing, we propose a quantum algorithm for the problem class Exact Cover 3, which is a sub-class of 3-satisfiability (3-SAT) problems and NP (nondeterministic polynomial time) complete. We find a quantum run-time which is significantly faster than the square-root run-time $N\to N^{1/2}$ of the Grover algorithm.

items.title: Analysis of the Second-Harmonic Generation Process in Nonlinear Metasurfaces Based on Multiple Quantum Wells: The Approach of Nonlinear Current Density, and The Development of Boundary Conditions
items.summary: Using plasmonic metasurfaces integrated with nonlinear materials, such as multiple quantum wells (MQWs), has been an excellent solution to enhance nonlinear light-matter interactions. In this approach, a plasmonic resonator enhances the intensity of the fundamental harmonic within the MQWs region, increasing the strength of the intersubband transitions inside the MQWs.

items.title: General Noise Channels and Mid-Circuit Measurements for Pre-Trajectory Sampling with Batched Execution
items.summary: Many studies of quantum protocols require fast sampling of large amounts of measurement data from noisy quantum circuits, such as for training machine-learning decoders for quantum error correction. Exact simulation of realistic noise is expensive, while stabilizer-based simulators are fast but approximate, for example through Pauli twirling, which generally alters the output statistics.

items.title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
items.summary: Contemporary classical information processors integrate tens of billions of transistors printed on a chip, yet are fully controlled through comparatively few external wires. This is possible because data flows through hard-coded operations in step with a global clock and is steered by external instructions.

items.title: Imaging chiral snake states in a qubit array with programmable gauge fields
items.summary: Spatially varying magnetic fields steer charged particles along directed paths. Where a field reverses sign, particles follow snake-like orbits along the reversal line, in a direction set by both the field orientation and the sign of their energy.

items.title: Aharonov-Bohm blockade of complete reversal in coupled Rabi cavities
items.summary: When a common bias reverses two bistable fields, the system can pass through either of two single-reversal configurations on its way to the favored state. We show that interference between these two orders of reversal can block the final step.

items.title: Covering the Pauli Observables: Sampling Thresholds and the Design Effect of a Measurement Setting
items.summary: Quantum state tomography and shadow-based estimation rely on measuring Pauli observables. An experiment does not measure them one at a time: it chooses a measurement setting that assigns one of the bases X, Y or Z to each qubit, and a single run in that setting yields estimates of every Pauli observable compatible with it.

items.title: Stationary Quantum Time Series: Spectral Theory of Process Memory and Measurement Records
items.summary: Classical time series analysis converts temporal dependence into structure that can be learned from a single observed trajectory, through stationarity, ergodicity, spectral representation, and finite-memory models. Quantum experiments are naturally time series: every run is a sequence of interventions and outcomes, and the memory of an open system is written in its temporal statistics.

items.title: Critical--localized reentry under periodic spacer control
items.summary: Tracking a fixed fraction of a quasiperiodic spectrum tests whether repeated critical--localized alternation extends over a nonzero spectral weight. We find such alternation in a matched-dimer chain by varying only the spacer on-site energies and following a fixed interval of integrated-density-of-states (IDS) labels.

items.title: Spectral Engineering of Charge Localization and Work Reliability in Collective Quantum Batteries
items.summary: The performance of a quantum battery depends not only on how much energy it stores, but also on how rapidly useful charge can be restored after work extraction. We show how engineering the reservoir spectrum connects these properties in an interacting collective-spin battery.

items.title: QWeaver: Quantum Circuit Cut Workflow with MLIR-based Compiler, Runtime, and Weaver Hybrid Tasks
items.summary: Quantum computers available today are constrained by limited qubit counts and high noise levels, making the direct execution of large quantum circuits infeasible on a single device, and while quantum circuit cutting addresses this by partitioning a large circuit into smaller subcircuits for independent execution, orchestrating the full end-to-end workflow remains a significant programming challenge. In this paper, we present QWeaver, a task-graph-based programming and orchestration workflow framework for quantum…

items.title: Subsystem evolution in the history state formalism
items.summary: We present a relational framework for characterizing the evolution of quantum composite systems, based on the correlations within a history state describing the whole evolution relative to a quantum reference clock. While total system-clock entanglement entropy consistently measures the unitary evolution of the closed global system, a different picture emerges for the reduced state of an open subsystem, whose evolution is generally non-unitary due to environmental coupling.

items.title: Addressable transversal CCZ gates on almost good quantum LDPC codes and nearly optimal magic state protocols
items.summary: Assuming uniform subfield product expansion, we construct quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes with distances $Ω_ε(N/\log^2N)$ and at least $N^{1-ε}$ individually addressable logical CCZ gates on pairwise disjoint triples of logical qubits, for every fixed $0<ε<1$. With all logical qubits outside these triples initialized to $|0\rangle$, any subset of the corresponding logical CCZ gates can be implemented with a transversal physical CCZ circuit.

items.title: Parity Push Post-Selection with Soft Parity Constraints for Quantum LDPC Codes
items.summary: Post-selection lowers the logical error rate of a quantum error-correcting code by rejecting unreliable shots. For a code with $K$ logical observables, the logical gap, a standard post-selection criterion, involves $2^K$ logical classes, and existing approximations to it suffer from a non-convergence error floor or a shielding effect.

items.title: Hierarchical coupling in tripartite van der Waals cavity magnonics for a low-loss and tunable coupled-mode Hamiltonian
items.summary: One of the greatest merits of cavity magnonics (CM) is the ability to explore rich coupled-mode physics, driven by the large \textit{in situ} flux tunability of magnonic resonances and magnon--photon coupling. Meanwhile, van der Waals (vdW) magnets offer an ultra-compact and highly integrated implementation of CM without complex fabrication processes.

items.title: Chirp-stabilized charging of a two-level quantum battery
items.summary: Resonantly driven two-level quantum batteries (QBs) suffer from strong pulse-area dependence and energy backflow inherent to Rabi oscillations. To address this limitation, we propose charging of a two-level QB with chirped pulses.

items.title: Separating QMA from the QCMA Hierarchy via a Switching Lemma for Polynomials
items.summary: We construct a classical oracle relative to which QMA is not contained in the QCMA hierarchy. Our main technical contribution is a switching lemma for bounded polynomials, which provides a new conceptual viewpoint on earlier sampler-based arguments separating QMA and QCMA.

items.title: Renormalization and exact Bloch bands: the trigonometric Rosen-Morse model
items.summary: We study the trigonometric Rosen-Morse potential as an isolated singular well and as an exactly solvable periodic lattice. The potential combines inverse-square singularities with Coulomb terms of opposite signs.

items.title: Parisi Energy before Parisi Geometry in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
items.summary: The fractured low-energy landscape of spin glasses presents a notorious barrier to optimization. While high-depth calculations indicate that the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can approach the Parisi ground-state energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass, how it does so remains elusive.

items.title: Intra-thalamic coordination maintains arousability in slow-wave sleep
items.summary: Slow-wave sleep preserves the capacity for spontaneous or stimulus-evoked awakening despite reduced responsiveness, yet how thalamic nuclei coordinate to preserve arousability remains unclear. items.title: Connectivity from activity in spiking neural networks
items.summary: We show that a wide range of recurrent neural network models obey a simple set of equations tying synaptic connectivity and single-cell response properties to neural correlations. Our modeling framework considers networks in a stationary, asynchronous state and contains a broad class of synaptic filters, spiking nonlinearities, and random-plus-structured connectivity.

items.title: Pilot-waves and copilot-particles: A nonstochastic approach to objective wavefunction collapse
items.summary: We propose an extension to Schrödinger’s equation that incorporates macroscopic measurement-induced wavefunction collapse. We find that a hybrid between two leading approaches, the Bohm-de Broglie pilot-wave and objective collapse theories, accomplishes this goal in accordance with Born’s rule.

items.title: Squeezing and Decoherence of Axion Dark Matter
items.summary: Bosonic particles beyond the Standard Model, such as axions, are among the leading candidates for dark matter. If such particles have a small mass, they are usually described as a purely classical field.

items.title: Chronic hydrocephalus after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: a brain–CSF interface framework for mechanisms, conceptual states, and surgical management
items.summary: Chronic hydrocephalus following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) may be more usefully conceptualized as the cumulative failure of several interacting brain–CSF boundaries than as a single obstructed conduit. A purely mechanical model cannot account for inflammatory CSF secretion, delayed absorptive failure, impaired clearance, altered tissue compliance, or the heterogeneous need for permanent shunting, so we use a brain–CSF interface and compartment framework to organize these observations.

items.summary: Optical coherence is a well-established branch of physical optics in which the statistical properties of fluctuating optical fields are described in terms of correlation functions over continuous spatial and temporal degrees of freedom (DoFs). Nevertheless, in any practical setting, only discrete DoFs are ever accessible.

items.title: Symmetric dilations of multi-qubit Pauli channels and semigroups
items.summary: We explore the symmetry properties of Stinespring dilations of single-qubit Pauli channels, addressing both the generic case and the specific examples of phase damping and depolarizing channels. For each scenario, we derive the representation of the Pauli group acting on the Hilbert space of the environment.

items.title: A quantum-classical surrogate model for the collision operator of the lattice Boltzmann method
items.summary: We introduce a hybrid approach utilising a quantum machine learning surrogate model to approximate the non-linear collision dynamics of the LBM. It offloads the non-unitary operations that challenge pure quantum solvers.

items.title: Observing Bell inequality violation beyond the qubit bound in a spinor Bose-Einstein condensate
items.summary: Correlations allowed by quantum mechanics can defy any classical explanation, with Bell nonlocality standing as their most profound and operationally powerful manifestation. While nonlocality has been demonstrated across a wide range of platforms, in many-body systems it has remained limited to ensembles of qubits, leaving the observation of higher-dimensional multipartite Bell correlations an open challenge.

items.title: Parameter-shift rules for gradients in boson sampling experiments
items.summary: Abstract Using a robust photon loss model for photonic quantum experiments, we derive n th order parameter-shift rules (PSRs) for computing gradients of Fock boson sampling transition probabilities where n photons are sent into a lossy interferometer. We also show that one cannot naturally generalize this gradient recipe to the case of Gaussian boson sampling.

items.title: The entangled loop: Emotion, interference and hierarchy in the architecture of consciousness
items.summary: Why does consciousness feel like something, and why is experience unified rather than fragmented? We propose that these properties arise from an entangled trefoil of emotion, interference-based inference and hierarchical orchestration, shaped by the thermodynamic constraint that living systems must remain far from equilibrium using limited energy.

items.title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
items.summary: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound.

items.title: Time-Division Multiplexing: The Operational Rhythm and Temporal Organization Layer of Digital Life
items.summary: Continual agents must handle urgent interaction while retaining alternatives, replaying errors, and committing safe long-term changes. A previous digital-life framework distinguishes online (busy) and offline (idle) channels, but leaves open whether these are separate programs or phases of a common process and how their operations should be ordered.

items.title: A systems-level energetic framework for conscious processing: energetic organization as a constraint on large-scale neural integration
items.summary: Conscious processing is associated with coordinated interactions among distributed neural systems, yet the biological constraints that enable and sustain large-scale neural integration remain incompletely understood. Contemporary theories emphasize computational, informational, and network mechanisms, while the potential contribution of systems-level energetic organization has received comparatively less explicit theoretical attention.

items.title: Multi-particle quantum walk search on a two-dimensional lattice
items.summary: In the present paper we study the formulation of a search problem and the efficiency of multi-particle quantum walk search algorithms. The discrete-time evolution of each particle in space is treated according to Grover's quantum walk evolution operator.

items.title: Residual Entanglement vs. Residual Coherence: A Wave Packet Approach in Neutrino Oscillation with Matter
items.summary: In this work, we investigate quantum correlations in three-flavor neutrino oscillations beyond the standard plane-wave (PW) description by employing a wave-packet formalism in the presence of constant matter density. We study three quantum correlation measures, namely the residual $l_1$-norm coherence, Concurrence Fill, and Three-$π$ entanglement, and express them in terms of transition probabilities for an initial muon-flavor state.

items.title: Attention Renders Sensory Contents into Conscious State via Content-invariant Frontal-Posterior Coupling in Humans
items.summary: Abstract Although attention promotes conscious perception, how it does so remains unclear. Human neuroimaging research has richly characterized attentional modulation upon visual processing, yet it remains unclear which of its components act as precursors of consciousness, which constitute consciousness itself, and which merely reflect post-perceptual, response-related operations.

items.title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment
items.summary: Motor responses evoked by noxious stimulation are used to assess neurological function in hospitalized patients with disorders of consciousness. In standard bedside assessments, these stimuli are applied manually, resulting in substantial variation in force, duration, frequency, and location.
